tasks.description:
You are modifying the Nexus repository itself.

Your objective is to transform the existing DeepSeek Harness frontend into a distinct, polished Nexus-branded interface while preserving all current behavior.

## PRODUCT IDENTITY

The product name is:

NEXUS

Nexus is an AI engineering harness and deterministic development controller. It must feel like its own professional developer product, not a reskinned DeepSeek Harness.

The visual direction should resemble a premium modern developer tool such as Linear, Raycast, Cursor, or a restrained mission-control interface.

Avoid:

* gamer aesthetics
* excessive glow
* excessive gradients
* excessive glassmorphism
* large decorative elements
* unnecessary animations
* visual clutter

The interface should feel:

* technical
* precise
* compact
* premium
* calm
* powerful

## VISUAL SYSTEM

Target visual palette:

Main background:
#09090B

Sidebar:
#0D0D10

Surface:
#111116

Elevated surface:
#17171D

Border:
#27272F

Primary text:
#F5F5F7

Secondary text:
#A1A1AA

Muted text:
#71717A

Primary Nexus accent:
#7C5CFF

Primary accent hover:
#9177FF

Secondary accent:
#49C6E5

Success:
#32D583

Warning:
#F5A524

Error:
#F04438

These colors are DESIGN INTENT, not instructions to hardcode these values repeatedly.

Inspect the existing DSH theme architecture and map the design onto semantic theme tokens wherever possible.

Use:

* compact spacing
* approximately 8–10px surface radius
* subtle borders
* minimal shadows
* smooth 120–180ms transitions
* strong hierarchy
* existing/system typography unless there is a strong reason to change it

## BRANDING

Replace visible DeepSeek Harness / DSH branding with Nexus branding where this represents the host application.

Examples include:

* sidebar product identity
* application name
* browser title where practical
* favicon where practical
* visible default product labels

Do NOT rename upstream package names, APIs, internal identifiers, npm packages, or technical dependencies merely for cosmetic reasons.

The installed DeepSeek Harness is an implementation dependency. Nexus is the product presented to the user.

### Sidebar

The sidebar identity should become approximately:

[geometric Nexus mark] NEXUS

Do not permanently use the DeepSeek fish logo.

A simple temporary geometric mark is acceptable if a final Nexus SVG does not yet exist.

Prefer the existing official sidebar branding slots such as:

sidebar.brand.mark
sidebar.brand.name

over modifying the sidebar implementation directly.

## ARCHITECTURAL RULES

This requirement is critical.

DO NOT treat app/node_modules as Nexus source code.

You MAY inspect files under app/node_modules to understand the installed DeepSeek Harness UI.

You MAY patch generated/installed files as part of an automated installation step when no supported extension mechanism exists.

But all permanent Nexus customization logic MUST be stored in source-controlled Nexus files.

Use this priority order:

1. official DSH extension points / slots
2. theme tokens / supported configuration
3. Nexus-owned UI/plugin code
4. small deterministic post-install patches
5. direct upstream structural patching only when no cleaner option exists

Do not create fragile broad string replacements when a supported extension exists.

All patches must:

* be deterministic
* be idempotent
* fail clearly when the expected upstream structure changes
* never silently corrupt installed code

## INSTALLATION PERSISTENCE

A fresh Nexus installation must automatically recreate the branded UI.

Running npm ci must not permanently destroy Nexus customization.

Create an appropriate source-controlled structure, for example:

ui/
branding/
theme/
overrides/

and/or:

scripts/
Patch-NexusUi.ps1

The exact structure is your decision after inspecting the architecture.

Integrate the Nexus UI customization into the existing setup process AFTER dependencies are installed.

The installation flow should conceptually become:

install pinned runtime
→ npm ci
→ apply required Control Room compatibility patch
→ apply Nexus UI branding/theme customization
→ continue setup

Do not duplicate responsibilities that can be implemented using existing plugin/slot mechanisms.

## PHASE 1 SCOPE

This task is PHASE 1 only.

Implement:

1. Nexus application branding
2. Nexus sidebar branding
3. Nexus dark visual theme
4. buttons and interactive states
5. inputs and composer styling
6. cards / surfaces / dialogs where controlled by theme
7. active navigation state
8. hover state
9. focus state
10. consistent spacing and border treatment
11. application title/favicon if practical without fragile architecture
12. mode-selection UI styling so it visually belongs to Nexus

Do NOT implement major new functionality.

Do NOT yet add:

* controller telemetry panel
* task dashboard
* cost dashboard
* new routing logic
* new controller behavior
* major navigation architecture changes

Those belong to later Nexus UI phases.

## EXISTING FUNCTIONALITY

All existing behavior must remain operational, including:

* session creation
* workspace selection
* conversation UI
* mode switching
* Normal Engineering mode
* DeepSeek Only mode
* settings
* model synchronization
* existing Nexus controller integration
* launcher behavior
* DeepSeek execution
* optional Codex review
* restart behavior

A visual redesign is NOT allowed to regress functional behavior.

## UPSTREAM COMPATIBILITY

The pinned DSH version should remain the implementation base.

Before changing anything:

1. inspect the installed UI packages
2. identify the global theme architecture
3. identify existing branding slots
4. identify where application metadata/title/favicon originates
5. identify which desired changes require patches and which do not

Document these decisions briefly.

Do not guess upstream paths or structures.

## IMPORTANT EXISTING INSTALLER ISSUES

Be aware of previous fresh-install problems:

* the portable Node runtime needs to be available on PATH for npm lifecycle scripts that invoke bare `node`
* PowerShell CRLF vs installed JavaScript LF can break exact multiline patch matching

Do not reintroduce either problem.

Any new patch logic must normalize or otherwise safely handle line endings.

## IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY

Prefer a small maintainable Nexus customization layer over a large fork.

Where possible, expose values centrally so future Nexus redesigns do not require modifying many files.

Avoid scattered magic values.

Keep branding/theme logic separated from controller/runtime logic.

Do not modify unrelated backend/controller behavior.

## VERIFICATION

After implementing the redesign:

Run all relevant existing Nexus tests.

Also verify at minimum:

* Nexus setup logic still succeeds
* Nexus branding customization is applied
* branding patch can be run twice safely
* DeepSeek fish is not used as the visible Nexus brand fallback
* NEXUS is visible as the application identity
* mode switching still works
* Normal Engineering still launches
* DeepSeek Only still launches
* settings still open
* session creation still works
* no startup errors are introduced

If practical, add deterministic checks to aih-doctor or the existing test suite that verify the Nexus UI customization is installed.

## WORKFLOW

Before editing:

1. inspect relevant code
2. map requested changes to existing DSH extension points
3. state a concise implementation plan
4. make the smallest maintainable implementation
5. run targeted verification
6. inspect git diff
7. fix regressions before declaring completion

Do not rewrite large upstream UI packages unless necessary.

## SUCCESS CRITERIA

This task is complete when:

* the application visually identifies as Nexus, not stock DeepSeek Harness
* the DeepSeek fish is no longer the visible product mark
* the application has a coherent Nexus dark visual system
* functionality is unchanged
* customizations survive reinstall / npm ci through Nexus-owned source-controlled logic
* patches are deterministic and idempotent
* tests pass
* the implementation is maintainable enough to continue with Phase 2 later

When finished, provide:

1. architecture decisions made
2. files added
3. files changed
4. how branding is applied
5. how theme customization is applied
6. which upstream areas still require patches
7. verification performed
8. any limitations remaining for Phase 2

# TASK — Nexus UI Phase 2: Live Controller Panel

You are modifying the Nexus repository itself.

Phase 1 and Phase 1.5 are complete. Nexus already has its own branding, theme, logo, compact sidebar, polished composer, mode selector styling, and persistent post-install UI customization.

Do not redesign those areas again unless a small integration adjustment is necessary.

Your objective for Phase 2 is to expose the actual Nexus deterministic controller inside the web interface.

---

# PRODUCT GOAL

Nexus should no longer look like merely a branded chat harness.

The UI should communicate what Nexus is actually doing:

* which task is active
* which execution class is running
* which model is executing
* which attempt is active
* whether verification is passing
* whether Codex review has been used
* how much context is being consumed
* what Git state has changed
* whether the controller is working, verifying, waiting, failed, or complete

This must be based on REAL Nexus state.

Do not create fake/demo telemetry.

---

# TARGET LAYOUT

Add a right-side Controller panel to active engineering sessions.

Conceptually:

```text
┌────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│            │                                     │ CONTROLLER  ● WORKING│
│  NEXUS     │                                     │                      │
│            │         Conversation                │ Executor             │
│ Workspaces │                                     │ DeepSeek V4 Flash    │
│ Sessions   │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Execution Class      │
│            │                                     │ deepseek_normal      │
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Task                 │
│            │                                     │ TASK-0042            │
│            │                                     │ Fix BLE reconnect    │
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Attempt         2 / 3│
│            │                                     │ ███████████░░        │
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Verification    2 / 2│
│            │                                     │ █████████████ ✓      │
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Codex Reviews       0│
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Context              │
│            │                                     │ 18.4k / 200k         │
│            │                                     │                      │
│            │                                     │ Git                  │
│ Settings   │                                     │ main   +23   -11     │
└────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘
```

The exact implementation may differ based on available DSH layout extension points.

---

# DESIGN

The panel must visually belong to the existing Nexus design system.

Use the existing Nexus tokens.

Do not introduce a separate visual system.

Target:

* width approximately 300–340px
* dark Nexus surface
* subtle left border
* compact developer-tool density
* no giant cards
* no excessive glow
* no glassmorphism
* violet used for active/controller state
* green only for success
* amber for waiting/retry
* red for failure
* muted neutral state when idle

Prefer grouped sections separated by spacing/dividers rather than wrapping every value in a card.

---

# PANEL HEADER

Top section:

```text
CONTROLLER                        ● WORKING
```

Possible controller states:

```text
IDLE
STARTING
WORKING
VERIFYING
REVIEWING
REPAIRING
WAITING
COMPLETE
FAILED
```

Do not invent controller semantics.

Map existing real Nexus state into the smallest truthful set of display states.

Each state should have:

* text
* small status indicator
* semantic color
* optional subtle animation ONLY while actively working

Do not use distracting continuous animations.

---

# REQUIRED DATA

Expose as much of the following as is actually available.

## 1. Executor

Example:

```text
Executor

DeepSeek V4 Flash
MAX
```

Show:

* provider/model
* reasoning level when available

Do not display duplicated strings such as:

```text
DeepSeek V4 Flash MAX Max
```

Reasoning level should preferably be a small badge.

---

## 2. Execution class

Display the real controller execution class, for example:

```text
deepseek_normal
deepseek_deep
codex_review
codex_solve
deterministic
```

This should be READ ONLY.

Do not turn this into a user-editable model selector.

The deterministic controller owns routing.

---

## 3. Task

Display:

```text
TASK-0042

Fix BLE reconnect issue
```

Use the actual active task record.

If there is no controller-managed task:

```text
No managed task
```

Do not fabricate a task from the chat title.

---

## 4. Attempt

Show current attempt information when available.

Example:

```text
Attempt

2 / 3
██████████░░
```

If Nexus does not have a meaningful maximum-attempt concept, DO NOT invent `/ 3`.

Instead display:

```text
Attempt 2
```

Truthfulness is more important than matching the mockup.

---

## 5. Verification

Display deterministic verification information.

Example:

```text
Verification

2 / 2 checks passed
██████████████ ✓
```

Possible useful states:

```text
Not run
Running
Passed
Failed
Partially passed
```

When useful, show compact individual checks:

```text
✓ Typecheck
✓ Tests
✕ Lint
```

Do not dump large command output into this panel.

Detailed verification artifacts should remain where Nexus currently stores them.

---

## 6. Codex review

Display:

```text
Codex Reviews
0
```

or:

```text
Codex Reviews
1

2 findings
```

Important:

Codex usage must remain informational here.

This UI must NOT make Codex the parent agent.

Do not change Nexus routing policy.

Do not automatically trigger Codex because the panel exists.

---

## 7. Context

When real values exist, display something like:

```text
Context

18.4k / 200k tokens
████░░░░░░░
```

Use actual current/budgeted context data.

If the true maximum is not known:

```text
18.4k tokens
```

Do not invent token limits.

If useful and available, include:

```text
12 files
18.4k tokens
```

Keep this compact.

---

## 8. Git summary

Show current project Git state.

Example:

```text
Git

main

3 files changed

+23    -11
```

Potentially include:

```text
Modified
3

Untracked
1
```

Do not run expensive Git operations continuously.

Use an appropriate refresh/event strategy.

Do not make any Git modifications from this display component.

This is read-only telemetry.

---

# OPTIONAL SECONDARY DATA

Only add these if they are readily available and useful:

```text
Elapsed time
Cost proxy
Input tokens
Cached tokens
Output tokens
Failure signature
Base commit
Worktree branch
Review required
Current verification stage
```

Avoid turning the panel into a telemetry dump.

Prefer the most useful engineering information.

---

# REAL DATA ONLY

This rule is critical.

NO:

* hardcoded TASK-0042
* fake token counts
* demo verification numbers
* random progress bars
* simulated statuses
* mocked Git changes

If a value is unavailable, show:

```text
—
```

or omit that row.

---

# DATA SOURCES

Inspect existing Nexus architecture before implementing anything.

Relevant state may already exist in areas such as:

```text
<workspace>/.ai-harness/state/
<workspace>/.ai-harness/runs/<task-id>/
data/routing/
data/completion/
telemetry.json
controller state
launcher state
verification artifacts
Git repository state
```

These are examples based on the existing Nexus architecture.

Do not assume exact schema.

Inspect the current implementation and reuse the authoritative source of truth.

---

# ARCHITECTURE

Do NOT couple React UI components directly to arbitrary filesystem implementation details if a clean bridge is possible.

Preferred architecture:

```text
Nexus Controller State
        │
        ▼
read-only controller/status adapter
        │
        ▼
small structured UI state
        │
        ▼
Nexus Controller Panel
```

For example, create a normalized read-only object conceptually similar to:

```json
{
  "status": "working",
  "task": {
    "id": "TASK-0042",
    "description": "Fix BLE reconnect issue"
  },
  "execution": {
    "class": "deepseek_normal",
    "provider": "deepseek",
    "model": "deepseek-v4-flash",
    "reasoning": "max",
    "attempt": 2
  },
  "verification": {
    "status": "passing",
    "passed": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "total": 2
  },
  "review": {
    "codexCalls": 0
  },
  "context": {
    "tokens": 18400
  },
  "git": {
    "branch": "main",
    "filesChanged": 3,
    "insertions": 23,
    "deletions": 11
  }
}
```

This is ONLY an architectural example.

Use actual Nexus schemas.

Do not introduce duplicate authoritative state.

---

# LIVE UPDATES

The panel should update while Nexus works.

Use the cleanest mechanism supported by the existing architecture.

Possible strategies include:

* existing runtime events
* existing session/controller events
* small backend read-only endpoint
* file watcher
* bounded polling as a fallback

Priority:

```text
existing event stream
→ proper read-only adapter/endpoint
→ filesystem watch
→ conservative polling
```

Do not poll expensive operations multiple times per second.

If polling is necessary, approximately 1–2 seconds is sufficient for controller telemetry.

Git may refresh less frequently.

---

# PANEL BEHAVIOR

The panel should:

* appear during an active workspace/session
* remain useful after completion
* handle no-task state gracefully
* handle deleted/missing task records gracefully
* handle invalid telemetry gracefully
* never crash the main conversation UI

Make it collapsible.

Suggested behavior:

```text
expanded width: 320px
collapsed: small rail/button
```

Remember the user's choice if there is already an appropriate UI-setting persistence mechanism.

Do not invent a new settings system just for this.

---

# RESPONSIVENESS

On wide desktop layouts:

```text
sidebar | conversation | controller
```

On narrower windows:

either:

```text
sidebar | conversation
```

with Controller accessible through a toggle/drawer,

or collapse the Controller panel automatically.

Do NOT squeeze the conversation to unusable width.

Suggested breakpoint should be determined from the actual layout.

---

# INTERACTION

Phase 2 Controller panel is primarily READ ONLY.

Allowed interactions:

* collapse/expand panel
* open detailed verification artifact if an existing safe mechanism exists
* possibly copy task ID
* possibly expand Git summary
* possibly open existing task details

Do NOT add:

* manual execution-class switching
* arbitrary routing override
* "Call Codex" button
* manual completion override
* destructive Git actions
* task mutation controls

Those require separate product/design decisions.

---

# EXISTING FUNCTIONALITY MUST REMAIN INTACT

Do not regress:

* New Session
* workspace switching
* session switching
* Normal Engineering
* DeepSeek Only
* mode switching
* model synchronization
* conversation
* composer
* tools
* settings
* light/dark/system themes
* sidebar collapse
* DeepSeek execution
* verification
* optional bounded Codex review
* task ledger
* routing
* completion logic
* launcher
* restart

The Controller panel observes existing state.

It must not become the owner of controller behavior.

---

# UPSTREAM / NEXUS SEPARATION

Continue following the established Phase 1 architecture.

Priority:

1. official DSH slots/layout extension points
2. Nexus-owned UI plugin/component
3. Nexus-owned theme/CSS
4. small deterministic patch only when unavoidable

Do not turn upstream `node_modules` into source code.

Any required installation changes must be reproducible by:

```text
setup.ps1
```

after a fresh:

```text
npm ci
```

Any patch must remain:

* deterministic
* idempotent
* version guarded where appropriate
* CRLF/LF tolerant
* fail-closed

---

# TESTING

Add deterministic tests for the normalized controller-state layer.

At minimum verify:

## Empty state

No task:

```text
status = idle
task = null
```

Panel renders without errors.

## Active DeepSeek task

Real fixture/state produces:

```text
executionClass = deepseek_normal
model = DeepSeek V4 Flash
taskId = expected ID
```

## Verification pass

Correct passed/total counts.

## Verification failure

Failure is surfaced correctly without breaking UI.

## Codex review

Existing recorded Codex call count is shown correctly.

Do not actually call Codex in UI tests.

## Git

Correct branch and diff summary for a small fixture repository.

## Corrupt/missing state

UI degrades safely.

---

# VISUAL VERIFICATION

Verify at least:

* 1920×1080
* 1440×900
* narrower desktop window

Check:

* panel does not overlap composer
* conversation remains usable
* sidebar + controller can coexist
* scroll behavior is correct
* panel independently handles long content
* collapsed panel works
* dark theme
* light theme
* active state
* idle state
* complete state
* failed verification state

---

# SUCCESS CRITERIA

Phase 2 is complete when:

1. Nexus has a right-side Controller panel.
2. The panel displays REAL controller/task state.
3. Current executor/model is visible.
4. Real execution class is visible.
5. Current task ID/description is visible when managed.
6. Attempt information is visible when available.
7. Verification state is visible.
8. Codex review count/state is visible.
9. Context information is visible when available.
10. Git summary is visible.
11. Status updates while Nexus works.
12. Panel can collapse.
13. Narrow windows remain usable.
14. No controller behavior is owned or mutated by the UI.
15. No fake telemetry exists.
16. Existing tests still pass.
17. New state-adapter/UI tests pass.
18. Fresh setup remains reproducible.
19. Phase 1 Nexus branding remains intact.

---

# WORKFLOW

Before editing:

1. Inspect existing Nexus controller/task/telemetry schemas.
2. Inspect DSH layout extension points.
3. Determine where the panel can be mounted without fragile upstream modification.
4. Determine the authoritative source for every displayed field.
5. Produce a concise architecture plan.
6. Only then implement.

During implementation:

* make small changes
* run targeted tests
* inspect the real UI
* test active controller state
* test idle controller state
* inspect git diff

Do not attempt unrelated refactors.

---

# FINAL REPORT

When complete, report:

1. architecture used
2. authoritative data source for each panel field
3. files added
4. files changed
5. live-update mechanism
6. layout integration mechanism
7. responsive behavior
8. tests added
9. verification performed
10. any fields that could not be exposed truthfully
11. Phase 3 recommendations

Do not claim success for values backed by placeholder/mock data.

We are continuing development of the Nexus repository from a previous machine/session.

The previous conversation history is not available here, so reconstruct the authoritative context from the repository itself.

Do not modify anything yet.

Phase 1, Phase 1.5, Phase 2 and Phase 3 are complete.

Before continuing, inspect at minimum:

docs/nexus-ui.md
ui/nexus-controller/lib/status.cjs
ui/nexus-controller/lib/detail.cjs
ui/nexus-controller/lib/index.js
ui/nexus-controller/lib/client.js
tests/NexusControllerPanel.Tests.cjs
scripts/TaskController.ps1
scripts/Route.ps1
scripts/Complete-Objective.ps1
config/home.cordis.patch.yml

Also inspect the current:

git status
git log
data/routing/
.ai-harness/state/

Treat the repository, tests, task ledger and docs/nexus-ui.md as authoritative. Do not try to reconstruct implementation details from assumptions.

Important existing architecture:

Phase 2 compact Controller is implemented through shell.overlay.
Native DSH details / conversation.details.tool must remain untouched.
Compact state endpoint is /nexus/controller.json.
Phase 3 Task Control Room uses /nexus/control-room.json.
Compact polling remains lightweight.
Root executor is distinct from review/escalation decisions.
GUI attempt = 0 currently renders as — because GUI execution does not yet enter the controller attempt lifecycle.
UTF-8 Windows PowerShell ledger boundaries have already been repaired and must not regress.
Phase 3 is read-only.

Read the repository and give me a concise summary of the current architecture, current Git state, and any discrepancies you find.

Do not edit anything until that reconstruction is complete.
